clue.text: One's charged for transport

parts.note: charged reads as paid for a fare, but means filled with electricity from a battery

explanation.surface: Someone is billed for a ride somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' suggests a fee, but the vehicle meant is one whose battery is charged.
explanation.definitionFit: A battery-powered motor vehicle is plugged in and charged before it carries people about.

clue.text: What could be laciest piece of stretchy material

indicators.note: says the word laciest could become the answer once its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks which stretchy fabric might be the most lace-like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What could be' is the anagram signal: the letters of LACIEST are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic is a rubbery band or cord that stretches and springs back.

clue.text: Headless chaps, almost totally sloshed — a feature of American sport

indicators.note: the word for chaps loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: chaps are men

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped from the word for sloshed

parts.note: totally sloshed means drunk

explanation.surface: Some drunken men somehow linked to an American game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headless' takes M from MEN to leave EN; 'almost' takes K from DRUNK to leave DRUN.
explanation.definitionFit: In American football, a play where the ball carrier sweeps wide around the defensive line is called this.

clue.text: It enables one to get an angle on the situation

definitions.text: It enables one to get an angle on the situation

parts.words: It enables one to get an angle on the situation
parts.note: getting an angle on a situation sounds like understanding it, but here literally means measuring angles of a site

explanation.surface: Something that helps a person see a matter from a new perspective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angle' is taken literally: the instrument measures horizontal and vertical angles in surveying land.
explanation.definitionFit: A surveyor's instrument with a rotating telescope measures angles across a site.

clue.text: Small container brought up in morning

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the picked letters read upwards, backwards
in signals letters lying inside the word morning

explanation.surface: A little box carried upstairs in the early part of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks ORNI from inside 'morning'; 'brought up' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: An inro is a small Japanese lacquered case worn hanging from a sash, for medicines or seals.

clue.text: Sort of Christian jazz fan about to embrace non-Christian festival

indicators.note: to embrace means to wrap around, so the festival sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast
C, short for circa, means about
Holi is the Hindu spring festival of colours

explanation.surface: A believer who loves jazz attends another religion's festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jazz fan' is old slang, cat; Holi is the Hindu spring festival of colours, and 'about' is C for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Roman Catholic Church is one particular kind of Christian.

clue.text: Soldiers with land vehicle — soldiers to leave, pull back

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a body of soldiers

indicators.note: to leave means the second lot of soldiers drops out of the vehicle's name

parts.note: a tractor is a farm vehicle used on the land
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: An army unit with farm machinery is told to withdraw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' takes OR out of TRACTOR, leaving TRACT. RE is the Royal Engineers and OR means other ranks, two standard ways of writing soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract is to draw in or withdraw, as a cat draws in its claws.

clue.text: Noble fellow with female relation by river

parts.note: a gran is a grandmother
the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

explanation.surface: An aristocrat goes with his grandmother to the river.
explanation.walkthrough: GRAN is followed by DEE, a British river.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee is a Spanish or Portuguese nobleman of the highest rank, or any high-ranking person.

clue.text: Big beasts somehow adapting as necessary originally

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are rearranged in some way
originally means the first letter of the word necessary is used

explanation.surface: Large animals managing to adjust to their needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes just the first letter of 'necessary'; the anagram signal then mixes that letter with ADAPTING AS.
explanation.definitionFit: These large black-and-white Chinese bears are big animals.

clue.text: Went round rubbish deposited by an old rocker

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish
an gives A
a Ted, a Teddy boy, was a 1950s rock and roll follower

explanation.surface: Someone walked past garbage dumped by an ageing rock fan.
explanation.walkthrough: A Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress who loved rock and roll.
explanation.definitionFit: To have rotated is to have turned about an axis, spun or gone round.

clue.text: Smart maiden worked out way to decrease international danger maybe?

definitions.text: way to decrease international danger maybe?

indicators.note: worked out means the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A clever young woman devised a plan for world peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' signals rearranging SMART MAIDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Reducing nations' weapons is one possible means of lessening the threat of war.

clue.text: Surprises in a street when meeting dogs with no lead

indicators.note: when meeting says the pieces join up side by side
with no lead means the first letter is removed, a play on a dog's leash

parts.note: hounds are hunting dogs

explanation.surface: Someone in a road is startled by unleashed dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no lead' looks like a loose dog but removes H, the leading letter, from HOUNDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To astound is to amaze or shock greatly, so the verb forms match.

clue.text: People living nearby their pubs?

definitions.meaning: a British pub is often called one's local, so neighbourhood pubs collectively

explanation.surface: Neighbours and the bars they drink in.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is a person's nearest pub; the plural covers several of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both nearby residents and, in British slang, the pubs they frequent.

clue.text: Certain plays made morals uncertain

indicators.note: uncertain means the letters are unsettled, in no fixed order

explanation.surface: Some dramas left the audience's ethics in doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncertain' is the anagram signal for MADE MORALS, playing off 'Certain' at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodramas are sensational stage works with exaggerated characters, a particular sort of play.

clue.text: Nail in food

definitions.meaning: a small short nail with a broad head
food, as in hard ..., ship's biscuit

explanation.surface: A fingernail found in a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Hard tack is the dry biscuit sailors ate; tack alone can mean food.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a small broad-headed nail, and slang for food, as in hard tack.

clue.text: 'Orrible situation returning — flier gets round it — that brings relief

indicators.note: gets round means the flier's word encloses the other piece

parts.note: an aviator is a pilot, one who flies

indicators.note: returning means those letters are read backwards

parts.note: hell without its H, in the dropped-aitch style the clue's 'Orrible signals

explanation.surface: A pilot copes with a horrid mess and offers comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of 'Orrible tells you to drop the H of hell too, Cockney style; 'returning' reverses what remains and 'gets round' puts the flier around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that alleviates eases pain or distress, so it is a thing giving relief.

clue.text: Military post is set up in troubled period

indicators.note: in places the reversed piece inside the other
troubled means the letters of period are disturbed
in a down clue, set up means the word is is written upwards, reversed

explanation.surface: A garrison is established during a difficult time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges PERIOD into PREDIO, and the reversed 'is' sits in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A presidio is a fortified garrison, especially in Spanish-ruled America.

clue.text: Change regular pattern of succession with any number dropping out

indicators.note: dropping out means the number is removed from the longer word

parts.note: alternation is a regular back-and-forth sequence
N is the maths symbol for any number

explanation.surface: Altering a fixed order of succession when people drop out.
explanation.walkthrough: N, standing for an unspecified number, is taken out of ALTERNATION.
explanation.definitionFit: An alteration is a modification, the act or result of making something different.

clue.text: Volunteers, smart, needed for sampling wine?

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
to smart is to sting with pain

explanation.surface: Clever helpers are required to try wines.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time volunteer reserve; 'smart' is the verb meaning sting, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine tasting is an event where wines are sampled; the question mark marks it as an example.

clue.text: Home west of California? His home's way south of there!

definitions.text: His home's way south of there!

indicators.note: in an across clue, west of puts the first piece to the left of the second

parts.note: in means at home
CA is the postal abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: A house lies west of California, while someone's own home is far south of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the pieces: an Inca's home in Peru lies far south of California.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas were the Andean people of Peru, a land far to the south of California.

clue.text: 'Nervy', tense inside, sitting on the fence?

indicators.note: inside places the tense letter within the nerve word

parts.note: neural means relating to nerves
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A jittery, anxious person who will not take sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nervy' is taken as 'of the nerves' (NEURAL), not jumpy; T for tense goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting on the fence is an idiom for refusing to take sides, being impartial.

clue.text: Snack — hopeless ultimately for giving to famous body-builder?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word hopeless

parts.note: Arnie is Arnold Schwarzenegger, the bodybuilder turned actor

explanation.surface: A useless snack handed to a celebrated muscleman.
explanation.walkthrough: A sarnie is British slang for a sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandwich, the commonest light snack, goes by this British colloquial name.

clue.text: Deal only half done — is America involved in neglect?

indicators.note: involved means wrapped up inside the other piece
only half done means just the first half of the word deal is used

parts.note: US is the United States

explanation.surface: A trade agreement left unfinished, raising the question of American negligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' looks like the verb or a bargain, but only its first two letters are used, as the outer shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Disuse is the state of no longer being used, a kind of neglect, both nouns.

clue.text: Pearl has shed tears in front of banker

indicators.note: in front of says the first piece comes before the second
shed suggests the letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: a banker in crosswords is a river, something with banks; the Ure is in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A girl called Pearl weeps before a bank official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' rearranges TEARS. A 'banker' is a river, here the Ure in Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl is something precious, a prized possession or a person greatly valued.

clue.text: Foreign city seen in October/November

indicators.note: seen in signals the letters lying inside the words October and November

explanation.surface: A city abroad visited in the autumn months.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the end of October and the start of November.
explanation.definitionFit: Bern is the Swiss capital, a city outside Britain.

clue.text: Second victory against England finally? The French cheat!

indicators.note: against means placed next to, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: a victory is a win

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word England

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: A second win over England sounds like French dishonesty.
explanation.walkthrough: S and WIN, then D (the last letter of England), then LE, French for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: To swindle is to defraud someone; both words are verbs about cheating people.

clue.text: Rite man devised in religious tower

indicators.note: devised means the letters are invented afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A man created a ceremony in a place of worship's tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised' rearranges RITE MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque from which the call to prayer is given.

clue.text: Water supply needed by land near building — large increase

indicators.note: needed by places the water supply after the grounds

parts.note: grounds are the land surrounding a building
a well supplies water

explanation.surface: An estate needs a well, perhaps a big addition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed by' joins the pieces with the water supply placed second.
explanation.definitionFit: A groundswell is a sudden rise in public feeling or support, a big surge.
